sources.title: Postwar Years
sources.note: occupation zones, Potsdam aims, Berlin blockade, currency reform, Basic Law and two-state founding. Scope: National synthesis; pair its chronology with exact legal sources and the atlas geometry audit.

sources.title: Germany in World Politics, 1945-1948
sources.note: U.S. zone geography; Bremen and Bremerhaven enclaves; occupation chronology. Scope: The article describes real administration; it cannot repair the atlas's coarse geometry.

sources.title: Declaration Regarding the Defeat of Germany and the Assumption of Supreme Authority
sources.note: opening declaration and four commanders' authority clauses. Scope: Formal authority text does not describe equal control or everyday implementation in every locality.

sources.title: The Four Powers in Germany, 1945-1990
sources.note: four-power authority, zones, founding of two German states, reserved rights. Scope: High-level chronology; use focused sources for daily life and local administration.

sources.title: Liberation and Occupation
sources.note: surrender, prisoners of war, displaced persons and Potsdam settlement. Scope: National account; individual experiences differed sharply by persecution, place and status.

sources.title: Denazification
sources.note: four Ds, removal policies, questionnaires and transfer to German tribunals. Scope: Museum overview; pair with evidence of limits and uneven outcomes.

sources.title: 5 March 1946: Law for Liberation from National Socialism and Militarism
sources.note: Spruchkammern, five categories, mass cases and declining support. Scope: Program-level history; do not infer one outcome for every defendant or community.

sources.title: War Crimes Trials
sources.note: International Military Tribunal dates, jurisdiction, defendants and judgments. Scope: Trial history is not a complete account of Nazi crimes, survivors, restitution or German reckoning.

sources.title: Subsequent Nuremberg Proceedings
sources.note: twelve U.S. proceedings, 184 tried, professional groups and judgments. Scope: Courtroom accountability reached only a small fraction of perpetrators.

sources.title: Basic Law, facsimile of the original document of 23 May 1949
sources.note: Article 3(2), original signed text and editorial introduction. Scope: A constitutional sentence states a legal principle; it does not prove immediate equality in homes, law or employment.

sources.title: Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany, official English translation
sources.note: Article 3(2) official translation. Scope: Current presentation includes later amendments; only the unchanged first sentence of Article 3(2) is quoted.

sources.title: Basic Law: equality in Article 3
sources.note: Elisabeth Selbert, Friederike Nadig and removal of the word grundsätzlich. Scope: Legislative history does not by itself establish later social outcomes.

sources.title: 14 August 1949: election of the first German Bundestag
sources.note: electorate, turnout, women candidates and first parliamentary tasks. Scope: Election statistics do not prove equal power or participation among all residents.

sources.title: Occupation Statute
sources.note: 21 September 1949 to 5 May 1955; reserved Allied powers. Scope: Reserved powers did not make West Germany identical to the earlier U.S. zone.

sources.title: Sovereignty
sources.note: Paris Treaties, 5 May 1955, remaining four-power rights. Scope: The Federal Republic gained broad sovereignty while four-power rights concerning Germany and Berlin remained.

sources.title: NATO member countries: Germany
sources.note: Germany joins 6 May 1955. Scope: Membership date does not describe public controversy, remilitarization or all security arrangements.

sources.title: Means of Survival
sources.note: rationing, hunger winter, barter, hamster trips, cigarettes and currency reform. Scope: Examples and national framing do not establish one diet or calorie level for every household.

sources.title: Everyday Life after 1945
sources.note: separated families, rubble, hunger, disease and hygiene. Scope: Broad synthesis; claims about groups or regions need more focused evidence.

sources.title: Housing Policy since 1945
sources.note: 1946 western-zone households and housing units; social housing policy. Scope: Western-zone totals do not describe the condition of every town or dwelling.

sources.title: Was ist Zuhause? A history of housing for children
sources.note: around 1950, pit toilets in yards and shared stairwell toilets. Scope: Illustrative national history; toilet arrangements varied by town, building, income and reconstruction date.

sources.title: Bathroom with gas-powered washing machine, 1957
sources.note: 1957 aspirational bathroom; washing-machine rarity in early 1950s. Scope: A publicity image shows aspiration and technology, not an average bathroom.

sources.title: A housewife in her new modern kitchen, 1957
sources.note: refrigerator ownership in 1955 and 1962-1963; gendered advertising. Scope: The image is aspirational and West German; it cannot stand for every household.

sources.title: Civil Affairs public health in occupied Germany
sources.note: food, shelter, fuel, safe water, disease surveillance and German health administration. Scope: U.S. Army institutional perspective; it records administration more readily than patients' experiences.

sources.title: Environmental sanitation in occupied Germany
sources.note: potable-water problems, sewer systems and local funding constraints. Scope: Administrative report; availability and safety differed between and within communities.

sources.title: Tuberculosis in occupied Germany
sources.note: tuberculosis section, mortality peak and control measures. Scope: Military medical reporting has uneven data and cannot measure every civilian's access to care.

sources.title: Hospital investment and structural history in Germany
sources.note: postwar bed destruction and 1950s investment backlog. Scope: National-sector history; it does not establish conditions in a named hospital.

sources.title: History of statutory health insurance
sources.note: restoration of self-government after 1945 and postwar financing. Scope: Insurance structure does not show equal access, quality or outcomes.

sources.title: Poliomyelitis epidemiology and vaccination in Germany
sources.note: inactivated vaccine available in West Germany from 1958; later oral campaign. Scope: The mass oral-vaccine campaign began after this card's interval.

sources.title: Democratization through denazification and education
sources.note: school reopening, teacher review, textbooks and reeducation. Scope: Policies and implementation varied by occupation zone and Land.

sources.title: Encounters in the Rubble: German Children and U.S. Soldiers, 1945-1949
sources.note: children's exchanges with U.S. personnel and unequal occupation setting. Scope: Project description signals themes; avoid turning encounters into a universal or sentimental story.

sources.title: Kloster Indersdorf displaced persons camp
sources.note: children's center, tracing, schooling, art and sports. Scope: One specialized center; it cannot represent all displaced children or camps.

sources.title: Foehrenwald displaced persons camp
sources.note: Jewish DP community, institutions, protest and family life. Scope: A major Jewish DP camp, not a proxy for all refugees, Germans or displaced persons.

sources.title: Flight and Expulsion
sources.note: numbers, camps, emergency quarters, private billeting and social tension. Scope: Use terminology carefully and do not detach German displacement from Nazi war and persecution.

sources.title: Women and employment in West Germany, 1949
sources.note: training, occupations, household expectations and Stuttgart context. Scope: Contemporary West German evidence with a specific setting; do not make it universal.

sources.title: Occupation and the Emergence of Two States, 1945-1961: introduction
sources.note: families, housing, women, equality law, occupation and state division. Scope: Broad period introduction; focused facts need their own sources.

sources.title: The academic success of mixed-race children, 1956
sources.note: school achievement findings and racist language in the original study. Scope: The period study uses racist categories and stereotypes; quote no slurs and foreground its bias.

sources.title: History of anti-racist movements in West Germany after 1945
sources.note: postwar racism, Afro-German occupation children and later activism. Scope: Long chronology; use only evidence securely tied to this interval.

sources.title: Economy and Society in West Germany
sources.note: housing, consumer goods, women, youth culture and social change. Scope: West German aggregate story; U.S.-zone local experiences varied.

sources.title: Guest workers in the Federal Republic
sources.note: 1955 Italy agreement, early occupations, recruitment and hostels. Scope: Later migration history must not project the much larger 1960s population backward.

sources.title: 14 August 1952: Equalization of Burdens Act
sources.note: levy, compensation, loans, housing and training aid. Scope: The program did not make losses equal or compensation immediate.

sources.title: The Economic Miracle
sources.note: growth, unemployment, exports, Korean War demand and labor conflict. Scope: The label miracle can hide policy choices, prior capacity, external demand and unequal gains.

sources.title: 65 Years of the Marshall Plan
sources.note: aid goals, implementation and scholarly debate over economic effect. Scope: Program totals and political intent cannot by themselves measure household benefit.

sources.title: A short event history of the 1948 currency reform
sources.note: Deutsche Mark introduction, initial allocation, price reform and social effects. Scope: Macroeconomic event history does not give one household outcome.

sources.title: History of the European Union, 1945-1959
sources.note: Schuman Declaration, ECSC and Rome Treaties. Scope: Institutional chronology does not capture all opposition, motives or social consequences.

sources.title: LeMO annual chronicle: 1954
sources.note: football World Cup, television family series and family allowance. Scope: Famous events and media milestones did not reach all households equally.

sources.title: New Beginnings after 1945
sources.note: licensed press, radio, parties, unions, local elections and cultural reopening. Scope: New institutions coexisted with censorship, personnel continuity and material shortage.

sources.title: LeMO annual chronicle: 1950
sources.note: rationing ends, First Housing Construction Act, ARD and Central Council of Jews. Scope: Formal endpoints and laws did not erase shortages or create housing immediately.

sources.title: LeMO annual chronicle: 1952
sources.note: Equalization of Burdens, Luxembourg Agreement, ECSC and school policy. Scope: Chronology selects headline events and does not supply complete implementation evidence.

sources.title: LeMO annual chronicle: 1955
sources.note: sovereignty, NATO, Italian recruitment agreement and education debates. Scope: Event chronology does not show identical local effects.

proposedOverrides.summary: U.S.-occupied German zone from 1945, then an outdated atlas label over part of West Germany through 1960.

batchIdentityNotes: Germany (USA) is an atlas occupation shorthand, not a sovereign polity, annexation, or citizenship category.
The historical U.S. zone included Bremen and Bremerhaven and excluded Tübingen; the exact atlas polygon does the reverse and also omits the U.S. sector of Berlin.
The Federal Republic began in 1949 under an Occupation Statute; the occupation regime ended in 1955 while agreed U.S. troop presence continued.
The 1960 switch to West and East Germany is a delayed atlas seam, not a fall or succession event.
